name: Leather Cloth Works
source: Author-supplied london_buildings_1891-96_corr_v1.gpkg (project extract west-ham-buffer-buildings-bng.geojson.gz); cached NLS OS London five-foot mosaic (os-london-five-foot-1893); EPFL OS text layer for the labels 'Leather Cloth Works' and 'Reservoir'
sourceCRS: EPSG:27700 to scene origin E538900,N183209; x east, z south, metres
method: Leather Cloth Works 3 October 2026: first models for site 865 (previously excluded as east of Channelsea). 45 of the 50 supplied OS outlines on the site are modelled, merged where they touch; the 3,838 m² northern outline is split into a main shed and its long arm. A hatched street block on the south road (OS lettering "STEPH…") that the GeoPackage omits is traced from the OS mosaic, moved into the GeoPackage frame by the measured (-1.75, +0.25) m offset, and split into three roofs. A small square opening in one range is read as a chimney base. All heights, storeys, roof forms, materials and functions are explicit estimates: the OS gives plan only and no Goad sheet or photograph of this works has been found.
evidenceNotes: OS labels on the site (EPFL text layer): "Leather Cloth Works" at about (372, -358) and "Reservoir" at about (417, -411). No "Chy.", boiler, tank or department labels.

The GeoPackage outlines at this site sit 1.75 m west and 0.25 m south of the printed outlines in the cached mosaic; the offset was fitted to the outline ink of 17 supplied footprints. Supplied outlines are used unshifted, as at Bromley; only the three traced roofs were moved into the GeoPackage frame.

Not modelled: fid 802028 (27 m², GeoPackage class "compound", drawn on the OS as a crossed outline at the junction of the great shed and the south-west yard, so it may be a covered way or open structure rather than a roofed building); fids 1088836, 1025151, 1113424, 1115301, 1230246 and 1291498 (0.8–5.3 m² posts, piers or yard fittings). fid 1061509 is the chimney base, modelled as a structure.
The reservoir is open water inside the works and is not modelled here; it is not part of the river water layer the builder checks against.
A grey stippled area on the northern OS sheet south-west of the great shed, at the sheet join, is not modelled: it has no supplied outline and its tone may be the sheet edge rather than a roof.

additionalBuildings.name: Leather Cloth Works — great northern shed
additionalBuildings.footprintEvidence: Source outline from the author's 1891–96 OS building GeoPackage (sourceFids 150), simplified at 0.15 m; checked against the cached NLS OS London five-foot mosaic (os-london-five-foot-1893). The supplied outline is one 3,838 m² shaded polygon with no internal lines on the OS; it is split here along the line of the north-east wall of its south-east arm, a modelling cut so that the arm and the main block take separate roofs. This record is the main block north of that line.
additionalBuildings.heightEvidence: Explicit estimate; no measured height, storey mark, Goad sheet or photograph of this building at c1900 is available. 1 storey, 5.5 m eaves: a large shaded works shed is read as one tall storey (a type-based reading: long single-storey sheds are a common works form of the period), not evidence about this works; 5.5 m chosen for realism.
additionalBuildings.roofEvidence: Ridge-and-furrow pitched roof with 4 parallel spans of about 10 m is an interpretation of a 40 m-deep single shed; no roof lines are drawn on the OS. North-light (saw-tooth) glazing would be equally plausible for a works shed but the renderer cannot draw the vertical glazed faces, so plain slate pitches are used.
additionalBuildings.functionEvidence: Largest roofed area of the works, beside the OS "Reservoir". Function (coating or finishing shed) is a type-based interpretation; the OS names only the works.

additionalBuildings.footprintEvidence: Not in the GeoPackage: this hatched (roofed) area of the OS sheet has no supplied outline, although its neighbours do (the GeoPackage stops at the east wall of fid 4408). Outline traced from the cached NLS OS London five-foot mosaic (os-london-five-foot-1893): hand-read wall lines snapped to the printed outline ink, corners taken at line intersections, then moved by (-1.75, 0.25) m into the GeoPackage frame (the offset that puts 17 supplied outlines at this site on the same ink) and clipped against the supplied neighbouring outlines. The OS draws no wall between this roof and the street range west of it; the division is a modelling cut (a line dropped square to the road wall from the corner of the open notch). The projecting room on its north side is the supplied fid 801184, modelled separately.
additionalBuildings.heightEvidence: Explicit estimate; no measured height, storey mark, Goad sheet or photograph of this building at c1900 is available. 1 storey, 5.5 m eaves: a large shaded works shed is read as one tall storey (a type-based reading: long single-storey sheds are a common works form of the period), not evidence about this works; 5.5 m chosen for realism.
additionalBuildings.roofEvidence: Ridge-and-furrow pitched roof with 2 parallel spans of about 12 m is an interpretation of a 24 m-deep single shed; no roof lines are drawn on the OS. North-light (saw-tooth) glazing would be equally plausible for a works shed but the renderer cannot draw the vertical glazed faces, so plain slate pitches are used.
